name: dTRINITY dUSD
oneLiner: dUSD is dTRINITY's USD stablecoin minted 1:1 against yield-bearing reserve stablecoins, with Curve AMOs and stability operations defending the peg.
collateral: Ethereum: whitelisted native stablecoin and yield-bearing collateral, including USDC, USDT, USDS, sUSDS, frxUSD and sfrxUSD, in isolated dUSD reserves. Fraxtal: frxUSD/sfrxUSD and other Frax-aligned USD collateral in isolated reserves. Katana: whitelisted USD stablecoins and yieldcoins in isolated reserves. Sonic: whitelisted USD stablecoins/yieldcoins such as frxUSD/sfrxUSD in isolated reserves. Each network deployment maintains fully isolated reserves with no cross-chain collateral sharing.
pegMechanism: Atomic 1:1 mint (no fee) and redemption (up to 50 bps fee) against whitelisted reserve stablecoins; Algorithmic Market Operations (AMO) pre-mint dUSD into Curve liquidity pools to programmatically support the peg; Stability Market Operations (SMO) buy back and burn dUSD from Curve when it trades at a significant discount; dUSD price is hard-coded at $1 in all protocol-internal operations to prevent oracle manipulation.

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: dUSD is atomically minted and redeemed against whitelisted dollar-stablecoin reserves, with AMO and SMO operations supporting liquidity.

obituary.epitaph: Subsidized borrowing that ran out of runway
obituary.obituary: dTRINITY launched dUSD in December 2024 as the debt asset of its subsidized lending market, minting it 1:1 against whitelisted reserve stablecoins and supporting the peg with Curve AMO and buyback operations. On October 29, 2026 the team announced it would sunset the protocol, saying it needed more capital to keep building, including defences against AI-enabled security threats, and could not raise it in the current market. The protocol kept operating for an orderly wind-down: redemption fees fell to 10 bps, dLEND interest rebates, Curve rewards and the points program ended, AMO liquidity was to be phased out, and the planned TRIN token was cancelled. Holders exit by redeeming reserve assets or selling on Curve; borrowers must repay before lenders and stakers can fully withdraw. About 1.31M dUSD remained outstanding at capture.
